stem.en: Kabir writes: CH4 + O2 gives CO2 + H2O. The teacher marks it wrong. Kabir says "but that is what happens when gas burns". Who is right?

text.en: Both. It is the right reaction and the wrong equation. Balanced, it is CH4 + 2 O2 gives CO2 + 2 H2O. As written it makes two hydrogens and one oxygen disappear.

feedback.en: They are. The counts are not. Four hydrogens go in and two come out.

text.en: The teacher, because methane does not burn to water.

feedback.en: Hold a cold steel plate over a gas flame and it fogs with water. Methane burns to carbon dioxide and water.

text.en: Neither, because burning is not a chemical reaction.

feedback.en: Burning is the most famous re-gripping there is. It is how Book I began.

explanation.en: The molecules can all be right and the equation still lie about the counts. Fix the numbers in front, never the molecules.
